conviction_note: The findings sum to +0.7: a small positive from IEEPA tariff refunds that the CFO said are left out of the Q1 and FY27 guide, and from Peloton's habit of beating the top of its own revenue guide, set against a Q2 holiday guide that has to lap the October 2025 hardware refresh and price increases. The scaled number is 0 (p_up 50 on a 13.5% absolute move) because the 25-delta skew pays 21 vol points for downside, the stock is up 16% over 20 days, and this name sold its August beat by 15.6% on the guide. Nothing I found outweighs the option market's lean. The gap between the two measurements is that skew and run-up discount.
bar: Company Q1 FY27 guide (Aug 6, 2026): revenue $545-565m (midpoint $555m), adjusted EBITDA $135-145m, gross margin ~57%, ending paid connected-fitness subscriptions 2.455-2.475m. Source: https://theclipout.com/peloton-q4-fy2026-earnings/ and https://sgbonline.com/peloton-delivers-soft-guidance-on-subscriber-losses/. Street revenue estimates from two sources roughly agree near the midpoint: $553.8m on Benzinga's page (quarter label unclear, via search snippet https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PTON/earnings-forecasts) and $558.28m on Earnings Whispers (via search snippet https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/PTON). EPS consensus is disputed ($0.14 Benzinga, $0.30 Earnings Whispers, breakeven on an undated Zacks page), so it is not used. The FY27 guide of $2.3-2.4bn revenue and $475-525m adjusted EBITDA came in below the Street's $2.43bn. The Q2 FY27 (holiday quarter) guide that this print will set has no sourced consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest 60,928,143 shares, 14.07% of float, 7.0 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15 (FINRA published 2026-10-26), down 9.5% from 67.3m in the prior period (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/PTON/short-interest/, fetched 2026-11-04). Mid-August it was 61.0-61.1m shares. Sealed baseline: 25-delta skew +21.44 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.33, ATM IV 176%, event-implied move 12.41%, run-up +15.98% over 20 days and +6.74% over 5 days, 26.6% below the 52-week high. Moderately crowded short that has been covering into the rally. The option market leans down on this print.

findings.finding: Peloton began receiving IEEPA tariff refunds after June 30 ($3m year to date as of the Aug 6 call). CFO Sid Thacker said 'we do anticipate receiving additional refunds, but we have not incorporated them into our forecast for the quarter or year.' The 10-K says refunds will be recognized when realized, so any received in July-September land in Q1 FY27 on top of the $135-145m EBITDA and ~57% gross-margin guide. The size is undisclosed: FY26 total tariff FCF exposure (all tariff types) was put at ~$30m, so the refund pool is plausibly in the low tens of millions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Peloton print carried a tariff refund. On EBITDA beats against its own guide (Q2 FY26 beat the top end by $6m) the stock still fell 25.7% on revenue and guide. EBITDA beats have not moved this stock; the guide has.
findings.why_not_priced: The refund is explicitly outside the company guide, and consensus EBITDA anchors on that guide. If it were priced, the Street would carry EBITDA above the $145m top end, and the downside skew would be smaller than +21 vol points. The path to the multiple: if refunds are booked and further ones expected, the FY27 EBITDA range ($475-525m) could be firmed or raised. Without that, it is a below-the-line-style one-off sized as a fraction.
findings.independence: 10-K subsequent-events note, a different document from the call: 'Subsequent to June 30, 2026, the Company began to receive refund payments for IEEPA tariffs previously paid' and refunds will be recognized 'when they are realized or realizable' https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001639825/000163982526000038/pton-20260630.htm

findings.finding: Peloton has repeatedly printed revenue above the top of its own range: Q1 FY26 revenue was $550.8m against a $525-545m guide and a $541.1m consensus, and FY26 revenue of $2.446bn finished $6m above its range. The exception is Q2 FY26, which missed its range by $8m on hardware sold to existing members. A repeat on a $545-565m range puts Q1 revenue near $566-570m, about 2% over the ~$556m Street midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-sell: Q4 FY26 beat revenue ($608m vs $597m) and EPS, and the stock fell 15.57% on the FY27 guide. Q1 FY26 beat and rallied +14.16%, but that came with a raised holiday guide. The reported-quarter beat alone has not decided the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Consensus sits at the guide midpoint, not above it, despite a habit of top-end beats. Since a beat lands inside what the company told the market to expect, the size is small.
findings.independence: Q1 FY26 revenue $550.8m vs $541.08m consensus (search snippet, prior-year data); Q2 FY26 miss of the range by $8m https://www.cfodive.com/news/peloton-cfo-departs-following-earnings-slump/811525/

findings.finding: On Sept 22, 2026 Peloton launched a refreshed Tread lineup, on sale in the US and Canada from Oct 1. It includes the foldable Tread Flex at $2,195, $1,100 below the $3,295 Cross Training Tread it replaces and the cheapest Peloton treadmill ever, plus the Tread Vision and Tread+ Vision with camera-based run coaching. The launch falls in Q2 FY27, so it bears on the holiday-quarter hardware guide, not on Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The October 2025 Cross Training refresh preceded a +14.16% reaction on the raised holiday guide in Nov 2025. The following quarter (Q2 FY26), hardware to existing members disappointed and the stock fell 25.72%. Product refreshes have helped the guide and then failed to convert.
findings.why_not_priced: The launch is public. What is not public is the first five weeks of sell-through, which management will color in the Q2 guide. A lower price point can lift units while cutting average selling price, so the sign is uncertain and the size small. No demand data (backorders, delivery times) was found either way.
findings.independence: Holiday 2026 Offer Match page lists Tread Flex, Tread Vision and Tread+ Vision as eligible products, consistent with the lineup being in market https://theclipout.com/peloton-offer-match-holiday-2026/ (same company source, not independent demand evidence)

findings.finding: The Q2 FY27 holiday guide has to lap a hard quarter. Q2 FY26 revenue was $657m, carrying the October 2025 hardware refresh and the Oct 1, 2025 membership price increase. The FY27 revenue guide midpoint of $2.35bn less the Q1 midpoint of $555m leaves $1.795bn for Q2-Q4, against $1.895bn in FY26 Q2-Q4 ($657m + ~$630m + $608m). That is a ~5.3% decline, steeper than the ~0.8% Q1 implies. The subscription price lap begins in Q2, and paid subscriptions are guided down ~9.8% YoY.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide has decided the last three prints. Aug 2026: below-consensus FY27 guide, -15.57% despite a beat. Feb 2026: Q3 guide $605-625m vs $638m Street, -25.72%. Nov 2025: raised holiday guide, +14.16%.
findings.why_not_priced: The FY27 total is public, but its quarterly shape is not. A Q2 guide showing a mid-to-high single digit decline could read as worse than the full-year -3.9% headline. The +21 vol-point downside skew suggests the market already fears this, which is why the size is small, and a 14% short float that is covering argues against sizing it larger. This is my arithmetic on public guidance, not a company statement about Q2.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 $657m revenue and the hardware miss to existing members (a different document): https://www.cfodive.com/news/peloton-cfo-departs-following-earnings-slump/811525/. The CFO tied the FY27 decline to lapping the prior year's subscription price increase (call summary via search).

findings.finding: Bloomberg reported on Sept 23, 2026 that Peloton held Goldman-arranged investor meetings for a possible ~$800m secured bond, its first traditional bond, at around an 8% yield. The 10-K puts the existing $1bn term loan's effective rate at about 10.2%. EDGAR shows no financing 8-K through Nov 4 (only an Item 5.02 on Oct 13), so the deal has not been executed. The CFO had said on the Aug 6 call that the company was working with bankers on a refinancing to lower its cost of capital.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The May 2024 $1.35bn holistic refinancing removed the 2026 convertible overhang. Its reaction is not in the baseline, so there is no comparable print.
findings.why_not_priced: Asking what the money buys: refinancing at roughly 8% against ~10.2% saves around $20m a year of interest and extends maturities. With net debt at $93m (0.3x net leverage) this is not distress. An announcement with the print, or an update on the deal, is a modest positive. A pulled deal would be a small negative, hence the wide range.
findings.independence: Secondary coverage of the same Bloomberg report: https://athletechnews.com/peloton-holds-talks-for-potential-800-million-debut-bond-deal/ (same underlying source). EDGAR 8-K list showing no financing filing: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001639825&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=10

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Upside reactions on this name have been large when the guide surprised up (+14.16% Nov 2025, +12.01% Feb 2025, +8.85% May 2026), consistent with short covering amplifying good news.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: some covering already happened in the run-up. What remains is an asymmetric tail on an upside guide surprise. It is not a directional call by itself.

findings.finding: Chief Accounting Officer Saqib Baig gave notice on Oct 8, 2026 that he is leaving for an external opportunity, effective Nov 27. No successor has been named, no disagreement was cited, and he gets no severance. It is the second senior finance departure in 2026, after CFO Liz Coddington left with the Feb 5 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CFO departure was announced alongside the Feb 2026 miss (-25.72%), and the two cannot be separated.
findings.why_not_priced: Already public for three weeks and minor. The 8-K's no-disagreement language makes it a governance footnote, not a signal on the quarter.

findings.finding: Insider Form 4s since the Aug print are routine: the COO's Oct 15 sale of 28,849 shares at $5.33 was tied to RSU vest tax, and the CAO's Oct 20 sale of 10,000 shares at $5.45 was under a 10b5-1 plan adopted Sept 2, 2025. No open-market insider buys were found.
findings.why_not_priced: These sales carry no information. They are filed because the absence of discretionary selling or buying is itself a data point.

findings.finding: For the holiday season Peloton is running an 'Offer Match' that matches a better offer on eligible equipment bought Nov 1-11, 2026. It covers Bike, Bike+, the Tread lineup, Row+ and the refurbished Bike, and implies an expectation of competitive discounting on its hardware.
findings.why_not_priced: Public but obscure. A price-match is a promotional mechanism, not a disclosed discount, so its effect on Q2 hardware average selling price is an inference.

baseline_tension: The positive findings (refunds outside the guide, a habit of top-end beats, short covering) cut against a +21 vol-point downside skew and a +16% 20-day run-up into a name whose last print sold a beat on the guide, so p_up is held at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs as fractions; the tariff-refund split went by guidance direction): refund finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6. It stays above a pure fraction because the CFO said refunds are outside the FY27 forecast, which gives a path to a firmed EBITDA range.
Lesson 1 and the guide-inside rule (6): reported-quarter beat pattern cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because this name sold its August beat by 15.6% and a beat lands inside what was guided.
Lesson 7 (crowded short against a negative; skew): Q2-guide negative cut from -1.0 to -0.8 for the 14% short float, and p_up moved from 51 to 50 for the +21 downside skew against a positive sum.
Left standing: Tread launch, financing (lesson 4: asked what the money buys, a cheaper refinancing with low net leverage, so a small positive), positioning, CAO departure, insider sales, Offer Match.
